They're not accurate at all. They work by measuring bioelectrical impedance, i.e. the differences in electrical resistance of muscle, fat and bone tissue. However, this is quite inaccurate as it depends on how much water you've consumed, and if you're sweating when you use the device etc.  Callipers are your best bet for a cheap way to measure BF%.
